name: mjpegtools
desc: Record and playback videos and perform simple edits
why: Old-school toolkit for manipulating MJPEG and MPEG streams at the byte level, a good door into video formats.

brief.what_it_is: A set of Linux command-line tools for recording video, playing it back, doing simple cut-and-paste edits, and MPEG-compressing audio and video. The homepage says recording works with Zoran-based capture cards such as the Buz, DC10, Matrox Marvel and LML33. Inputs include captured video and MJPEG AVI files (for example from xawtv, or DV converted with dv2jpg). Outputs include MPEG streams, including VCD and SVCD for hardware playback. The executables list (lav*, y4m*, yuv*, mpeg2enc, mplex and others) suggests a set of small programs that pass streams between each other, but the homepage does not document them individually.
brief.why_it_exists: The author describes the tools as aimed at interoperability with other video tools, so that MJPEG AVIs captured with xawtv or made with broadcast 2000 can be edited, played back and compressed. The homepage also presents them as a way to get MPEG output that plays on almost any player and OS.

commands_seen.context: From the Dec 2017 news item: how to check out the full SVN repository after SourceForge retired CVS commits. The homepage does not give a build command.

brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps. It points to source tarballs and RPMs on SourceForge, and a Windows MinGW build exists from a 2008 news item. Recording needs a supported Zoran-based capture card and its driver; the homepage links to driver pages for this. The news items mention a SourceForge download page for 2.2.1 and a Dec 2024 change that makes the jpeg library detection use pkgconfig.
brief.standout: The tools are old-school and interoperate through uncompressed YUV4MPEG streams, so each small program does one job in a pipeline. The homepage notes the mpeg2movie encoder was partly derived from an old snapshot of the mjpegtools MPEG encoder, which shows how far the code has spread. The scout note's claim that these work at the byte level is not stated on the homepage.
brief.status: Quiet, with some recent activity. The last tagged release on the news is 2.2.1 (Sept 10, 2021). The most recent news item is from Dec 2024: the tools moved to jpeglib 9f with pkgconfig, and lavrec was dropped from the build. A May 2023 meeting of active developers is also mentioned. The homepage layout was last modified April 2005.
brief.caveats: lavrec, the recording tool, is no longer compiled as of the Dec 2024 update, so older 2.x versions are needed for recording. Recording depends on old Zoran-based capture cards, several of which the homepage marks as discontinued. Windows support is partial: a 2008 news item says lavrec and audio output in lavplay did not work there. Ongoing development has been slow, and the homepage notes that the jpeg-mmx project was declared dead in 2006. The page also contains a broken link to linuxvideo.org. The executables list is long and undocumented on the homepage. Licence was not stated on the page.
quotes: The mjpeg programs are a set of tools that can do recording of videos and playback, simple cut-and-paste editing and the MPEG compression of audio and video under Linux.
A key design objective of the tools is interoperability with other video tools:
If you don't know where to start, please start by reading this document, it gives an overview of about everything the tools can do.
